We will now take a closer look at each of the key moves of Honsu Pumse.
Son-nal-deung-hae-cheon-mak-i is a technique to cross the two hands in front of the chest
and block by scattering them sideways.
When performing Momtong-hae-cheon-mak-i, the tip of the hand must not rise above the shoulder.

Mae-jumok-yang-yeop-guri-an-chigi is a technique to strike both sides of the waist outside in
with both fists elevated to about one fist length above the shoulder.
Attach the armpit firmly to the body to concentrate force.
The fist should be placed slightly over the elbow.
The elbows should be close to the torso.
Be careful not to let the fists rise excessively.
Godoro-kaljebi is a technique used to block an opponent's attack by pressing with the palm of your hand
and attack an opponent's neck with an arc fist.
Strike an opponent with the arched part of the arc fist.
Concentrate and transfer force by making the surface area of the target small.

Anpal-mok-are-pyo-jok-mak-gi is used to create a target at shoulder elevation with the arc fist of the hand performing aremak-gi,
where the inner wrist touches between the thumb and index finger to block.
It is important to fix the hand acting as a target in front of the lower abdomen and only move the arm blocking the lower body.
When performing seon-na-geun-gang-mak-gi, the hand blade and center line should be aligned.
Be careful not to let the elbow of the arm blocking the face rise first.
Gyeot-dari-seo-gi is a standing posture where one leg acts as support.
The opposite big toe touches the ground in the middle of the back of the supporting foot blade,
and the rear sole is slightly raised.
Both feet slightly touch each other and stand with the knees facing forward.
